ride.title: THE RIDE DOWN
pilot: Drop Two. Ninety seconds to the moon. Get your stories in.
Drop Two. Little turbulence. That's the bears waving.
Drop Two. Whoever's crying, it's echoing up front.
Drop Two. Ramp down in two minutes. Somebody talk, the quiet's worse.
Drop Two. Reminder: the Thunder Marines are the good guys. Carry on.
seat: Seat across: {who}. Last week: Pvt. Bell. Bears.
Seat across: {who}. The name tag's been crossed out four times.
Seat across: {who}. Third one in that seat this week.
Seat across: {who}. Previous occupant left half an antenna.
Seat across: {who}. Seat freshly wiped. Don't ask.
ride.next: Ramp down. Next seat, next story.

lines: Third moon I've liberated. Liberated it right down to the bedrock.
Command calls it landscaping.
Then the locals got upset. Over TREES.
landscaping.tag: Okafor did not see the problem. Okafor is no longer in a position to see anything.

lines: Lost my whole squad on Doren Two.
Not to the Wooka. To the cook.
Then the Wooka got the cook.
the-cook.tag: Lunch today is rations. Nobody is sure who made them.

lines: Perfect shot. Chieftain, two clicks, no wind.
Then something tugged my boot.
Something knee-high. It had been there the whole time.
perfect-shot.tag: Lindqvist aims with the other eye now.

lines: I built the orbital strike's off switch.
In six years nobody's asked me where it is.
Anyway. Bears ate the manual.
off-switch.tag: There is no off switch. Ruiz knows. Ruiz sleeps fine.

lines: Found a Wooka village. Empty. Little hats on every door.
Little hats. Little HELMETS, actually.
Ours. Snorkels still on.
little-hats.tag: The Wooka do not make hats. They collect them.

lines: One followed me for three days. Just watching.
Day two it brought me a fish.
Day three it brought me Cpl. Benn's helmet. I think it was being nice.
They hum. All night. In harmony.
Someone recorded it. Top of the charts back home.
Royalties go to a stump on Doren. Legal is furious.
the-humming.back: I've got it on my playlist.
the-humming.tag: Still number one. The Wooka have not been told.

lines: Wooka don't count past four.
One, two, three, four, lots, then 'shiny ones'.
Linguists say 'shiny ones' also means 'lunch'.
counting.tag: We are not a number. We are a menu.

lines: Night watch. Quiet. Too quiet. Then: hoo-ka.
Not from the trees. From INSIDE my backpack.
Never found out how. Never opened it again.
the-backpack.back: Is that... the backpack you're wearing?

lines: Squad went into the ferns. Comms fine. Everyone checking in.
Six voices on the net. Five Marines.
The sixth was REALLY good at it.
six-voices.tag: Orr checks in every ten minutes now. Nobody checks Orr.

lines: They don't take prisoners.
They take antennas. Then helmets. Then whatever's left.
Then they come back for the antennas they missed.
antennas.tag: Field Manual, page one: remove antennas before landing. Added last Tuesday.

lines: I've patched blaster burns. A walker on someone's foot.
Wooka bites don't patch.
They're very small. There are just very MANY of them.
We torched their nesting grove. Orders. Standard stuff.
So they came for our barracks.
Unprovoked. Out of NOWHERE.
unprovoked.tag: High Command remains baffled by the Wooka's attitude.

lines: A Wooka took my brother's helmet. With my brother in it.
Nine years I've hunted that Wooka.
It still wears the helmet. It looks GOOD in it.
the-helmet.tag: It does. It's been polishing the helmet.

lines: We salted their fields so they'd move on.
They moved on. Onto our supply depot.
Ate the salt. Then the depot.
the-salt.tag: Command calls it unrest. The Wooka call it Tuesday.

lines: Remember Second Squad? The ONE fluffy one?
They'd paved over its mum's stump. For a landing pad.
She's still out there. She remembers our helmets.
I retire next week.
A Wooka took my tags. There's a Wooka called Sato now.
the-name.tag: He has a better record than Sato.

lines: Don't look under the bench.
